best_for: Vim users who want built-in LSP, Tree-sitter and a Lua config, on Windows or Linux, and are happy to set things up themselves.

points.title: Vim habits carry over
points.text: Neovim keeps Vim's editing model and Vimscript, and Vim 8 plugins run. Your config can move to `init.lua` at your own pace.

points.title: Code smarts built in
points.text: A built-in LSP client handles code inspection and refactoring, and Tree-sitter gives accurate highlighting and text objects. You still pick and set up language servers yourself.

points.title: A terminal app by default
points.text: Neovim runs in a terminal. A separate GUI such as Neovide can wrap it, since any program can drive it through its API.

points.title: Windows: MSI or zip
points.text: The MSI installs machine-wide for x64 or Arm64. The zip needs no admin rights. Windows 7 and older are not supported, and a missing VCRUNTIME DLL means installing the Visual C++ runtime.

points.title: The Flatpak moves your config
points.text: Flathub's build reads its config from `~/.var/app/io.neovim.nvim/config/nvim`, not `~/.config/nvim`. It is not marked verified by Flathub.

points.title: Free, Apache and Vim licensed
points.text: Neovim costs nothing. The Windows listing keeps 28 versions; Linux lists only the current release. No Mac build is listed here; the project offers macOS archives and Homebrew.
